body:
Improves the lower bound for C_3c from 1.6747338950414058 (#185) to

C_3c >= 1.674894211307116

a gain of 1.603e-4. Markdown changes only.

Construction: (X, Y) = sum_i 55^i (x_i, y_i) over n = 10^20 independent digits, 39041372760532870645 of them with one law on 51 points of Z^2 and 60958627239467129355 with another on 47 points (exact rational weights). x - y is injective on each support and all five forms x - y, x, y, x + y, x + 2y are at most 27 in absolute value, so in base 55 every entropy is a sum over digits. Per digit (natural log):

    H(X-Y)  = 1.90144092556070111045748...
    H(X+2Y) = 1.13526031239715368784461...  (the largest of H(X), H(Y), H(X+Y), H(X+2Y), which agree to about 21 digits)

The weights are exact; the logarithms are enclosed in ball arithmetic and the bound is a truncation of the lower endpoint.

Certificate and two independent checks (python-flint; PARI/GP): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23289305

The PR also fixes the definition on the page: A ±^G rB now ranges over (a, b) in G. Read literally without that, the constant would be at most 3/2 (Plünnecke-Ruzsa and Ruzsa's triangle inequality), below every listed bound.

Done with an AI system I built; I reviewed the references and ran both checks.
